walkthroughs.body_html: Dickens wrote in response to the 1834 Poor Law, which forced the destitute into brutal workhouses. After visiting a ragged school in 1843 he aimed to deliver a 'sledgehammer blow' against indifference to poverty. The novella was an instant success and is still printed today.

The five sections are called staves because a stave is a stanza of a Christmas carol. The form signals that the novella is a song-like moral lesson, full of repetition, refrains and emotional swells. Stave 1 introduces Scrooge; Staves 2-4 are the ghosts; Stave 5 is rebirth.

Jacob Marley appears wrapped in 'cash-boxes, keys, padlocks, ledgers' - the chain he 'forged in life'. Dickens makes obsession with money a literal weight on the soul. Marley warns Scrooge that three more spirits will visit, beginning the redemption arc.
